agent_vs_you: The agent's tool choice was right (image-to-video of the supplied portrait, 5 s, 1:1, sound dropped) and its prompt asked for only a blink and breathing. Two things I would do differently: (1) give the portrait as BOTH start and end picture, the catalogue's own 'seamless loop' strength, so the model has to bring her face back to exactly where it started, which strongly damps the sideways drift it produced; (2) describe the only motions positively (she holds still, blinks once, one slow breath, locked-off tripod) instead of a list of forbidden motions ('no head movement, facial reshaping...'), which video models often read as cues. Its verification step could not work: check takes a picture, received the source and the clip, saw one image and flagged 'cannot verify', so nothing caught the sway.

your_plan.say: I'll bring the portrait to life for 5 seconds with one natural blink and a slow breath, camera locked off and silent. I'm anchoring the clip to your photo at both ends so her face can't wander.

params.prompt_or_change: Photorealistic, locked-off static camera on a tripod, square head-and-shoulders portrait. The woman holds her pose and her soft closed-mouth smile, looking straight into the lens. About halfway through she blinks once, naturally, and her shoulders rise and fall very slightly with one slow breath. Her head stays centred and still in the frame; her curly dark hair, grey knitted sweater and the park behind her stay exactly as in the photo, with only a faint breeze in the leaves.

steps.why: Start and end frame are the same photo: the model must return her to the original position and face, which suppresses drift and sway; the clip's invented sound is dropped by default.

fix: 1) Planner rule / catalogue line for image-to-video: 'a photo that should just come alive (blink, breath, hair in the wind) -> the same picture as start AND end, motion described positively, no list of forbidden motions'. 2) Harness: let check take a clip (sample 4-6 frames plus the source) and allow one regeneration on a drift or sway verdict; today it saw one image and could only flag. 3) Longer term, a driven 'portrait-live' tool (keypoint-driven blink/breath on the still, LivePortrait-style) that keeps identity and position locked by construction.
evidence: portrait-woman.jpg is a 640x640 head-and-shoulders photo (curly dark hair, grey knit sweater, park). portrait-animated.mp4 is 480x480, 5.17 s, 24 fps, no audio stream (silence correct). Block-matching the face region against frame 0 at 240 px scale: the face drifts left by 4 px at 1.0 s, 11 px at 2.0-2.25 s (about 4.6% of the frame width), comes back to 5-6 px and ends at 8 px, while the background patch stays at 0 shift: the camera is still but she sways sideways, which is exactly the judge's major fault. identity-check.json: 'Only one image is visible, so consistency ... cannot be verified.'
